Track each beam’s token history, cumulative log probability, and EOS state. Expand unfinished beams, retain the best normalized candidates, and carry completed beams unchanged. Length normalization uses generated length, including EOS but excluding the prompt. Stop when every retained beam ends or the token budget expires; stopping at the first EOS can discard a better unfinished hypothesis. Beam search is an approximate deterministic search, not sampling from the model distribution.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** A sequence score is $s(y)=\sum_t\log p(y_t|y_{<t},x)$; length normalization divides by a specified function of generated length. Beam search keeps only a limited number of partial hypotheses, so it can prune the eventual optimum. Increasing beam width changes search quality and compute, but does not automatically improve human-perceived output quality. [3](https://d2l.ai/)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://mlabonne.github.io/blog/posts/2023-06-07-Decoding_strategies.html) and [2](https://d2l.ai/chapter_recurrent-modern/beam-search.html).
